ideas.description: Change one thing in the E002 recipe: the epoch count, from 9 to 8.5. Scale the lr/lookahead schedule to the new total step count, so the shape stays the same over fewer steps. The last half-epoch uses the first half of that epoch's permutation. The final partial batch is still the shape that was compiled in build(). Everything else stays bit-identical to E002 (commit 479b9a3).
ideas.expected: Accuracy about 0.7535-0.7540, extrapolating linearly at the measured 0.31 pp/epoch from 0.7552 at 9 epochs. Time about 7.9 s, down about 5% from 8.34 s. Feasible means a new best and refutes H1.1.2, which predicted 0.744-0.752. If accuracy is below 0.753, the knee is between 8.5 and 9 epochs and the next step is 8.75.

ideas.hypothesis: H2.2 (proposed new Lvl3 H2.2.2: removing atomic-kernel ops from the non-conv path saves >=2% at identical accuracy)
ideas.description: Make one systems change on the E002 recipe at 9 epochs. Replace the final nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((1,1)) with x.amax(dim=(2,3)), or with x.flatten(2).amax(-1). Its backward then becomes a dense masked elementwise op that Inductor can fuse, instead of the atomic adaptive_max_pool2d_backward kernel, which takes 0.48 ms of each 18.8 ms step. Re-warm in build() for the full batch, the partial batch and eval shapes. Change nothing else.
ideas.expected: Time down 2-3%, about 8.15 s against 8.34 s. Accuracy within 0.1 pp of 0.7552, since only tie handling differs. That stays feasible and is a new best on its own. It also stacks with the 8.5-epoch idea.

ideas.description: Target conv throughput: cuDNN conv kernels are about 75% of GPU time but run at only about 30% of bf16 peak. On the E002 recipe at 9 epochs, set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True before warmup in build() and compile the model step with mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', so Inductor benchmarks its Triton conv/GEMM templates against cuDNN for every shape (full batch, partial batch, eval) on synthetic inputs. All autotuning stays in untimed build(). If the base already has one of these settings, add only the missing one.
ideas.expected: Time down 0-8%, most likely about 3%, with accuracy identical within 0.05 pp. Under 2% means the conv algorithms were already near-optimal, and the remaining systems headroom comes only from the non-conv ops.

ideas.hypothesis: H1.1 (proposed new Lvl3 H1.1.4: the inherited peak lr 9 is not optimal for CIFAR-100 at ~9 epochs)
ideas.description: Change only the peak learning rate on the E002 recipe at 9 epochs: lr 9 to 11.25 (x1.25). Keep the effective weight-decay strength lr*wd fixed, i.e. rescale the wd coefficient so decoupled decay is unchanged, and keep the warmup/decay shape and everything else identical. The lr was carried over unverified from CIFAR-10 airbench (D001).
ideas.expected: Two-sided probe; most likely the accuracy change is within ±0.3 pp and time is unchanged. A gain of 0.1 pp or more is real given E003's deterministic noise floor and is worth about 0.3 epoch (about 0.3 s). If accuracy drops, run lr 7.2 next.

ideas.description: Corrected version of I007 that changes only one thing. On the E002 recipe (bs 1024, 9 epochs, same schedule shape), optimize the 4D conv filters (all except the frozen whitening conv) with Muon: Nesterov momentum 0.6, lr about 0.24, 5 Newton-Schulz quintic steps in bf16, with the update scaled by sqrt(max(1, out/in)) on the flattened [out, in*k*k] matrix. BatchNorm biases and the head stay on the existing Nesterov SGD with the same lr/wd. Keep lookahead. Compile the NS loop in build(). Log the optimizer step time separately.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.2 to +0.8 pp at 9 epochs, worth 0.7-2.5 epochs of slack. NS overhead adds 3-6% per step. If accuracy is up by 0.4 pp or more and overhead is 6% or less, follow up at 8 epochs, where a net 8-15% time gain is expected. Accuracy within ±0.1 pp refutes H1.2.1 at this batch size.

ideas.description: Explore the airbench96_faster-style batch selection idea. Each step, draw 2048 examples and score them with a tiny proxy CNN (whitening plus widths 32/64/64, depth 1, trained online on the same selected batches with its own SGD). The main model trains on the 1024 with the highest proxy loss. Keep the same number of main-model steps as the 9-epoch base (432), so the main model's per-step cost is unchanged and only proxy cost is added. Compile the proxy in build().
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.3 to +0.7 pp at matched main-model steps. Proxy overhead +8-15% time. Net gain only if the accuracy gain is worth more than about 1.5 epochs. Most likely outcome: accuracy up, time up 10%, net neutral or worse at this horizon, which would weaken H1.4.

drop.reason: The E003 profile contradicts its premise. The step is not launch-bound: GPU time is about equal to wall time, and the SGD step is 0.44 ms of 18.8 ms. A fused optimizer or fully compiled step can save at most about 2-3%, well short of H2.2.1's 8% or more, and costs a lot of engineering. Better non-conv targets have replaced it: the atomic pooling backward and conv autotuning.

It changes two things at once: the optimizer (Muon) and the batch size (1024 to 2000, with a new decay schedule). D002 recommends testing Muon first at bs 1024 against E002. It is replaced by a single-change Muon idea at bs 1024 and 9 epochs. Batch 2000 can follow if Muon shows a signal.

structured_output.summary:
State: 9 epochs gives 0.7552 in 8.34 s (E002). Accuracy is deterministic given the seeds, and timing noise is about 1% (E003). The slope is about 0.31 pp per epoch, so the knee is near 8.3 epochs.

Changes to the queue:
- **Dropped I009:** the profile shows the step is not launch-bound.
- **Dropped I007:** it changed the optimizer and the batch size together. A single-change Muon test at bs 1024 and 9 epochs replaces it.

New ideas:
- **Top exploit:** 8.5 epochs. Expected 0.7535-0.7540 at about 7.9 s, which also tests H1.1.2 directly.
- **Systems wins at the same accuracy, guided by the profile:** swap the global adaptive max-pool for amax, removing an atomic backward kernel (about -2.5%), and autotune the conv kernels with cudnn.benchmark plus max-autotune (0 to -8%).
- **Hyperparameter probe:** peak lr ×1.25 with the effective weight-decay strength held fixed. The lr was carried over unverified from CIFAR-10.
- **Explore:** the corrected Muon test, and proxy-model hard-example selection (H1.4.1, untested until now).

Kept: I006 (lookahead ablation) and I008 (progressive resizing). I005 (LS 0.2) is still running.

The queue now has 8 queued ideas: about 5 exploit or high-information and 3 explore. Once the 8.5-epoch point and the pooling fix land, they should be combined.
